_comment: The launch checklist's row source (ADR-1001). No checklist row is hardcoded in the renderer;
every row comes from here, and a row with no `source_url` FAILS rather than rendering.
ADR-1001 is the reason the split exists: the design source recorded SIX required pages, and
the verified position is that Razorpay's default activation flow documents FIVE, with a
separate CONDITIONAL list for additional e-commerce sites. The built page set is the
seven-page superset; this file records which of them the provider actually demands, and
under what condition, so the checklist never presents a conditional requirement as a
The `card statement descriptor` row the plan carried was DROPPED at kickoff as unverified,
and it is not reinstated here on memory.
ALL ROWS ARE MANUAL in v1. The URL-fetch probe arm is designated cut #1 (PLAN, Appetite),
taken at kickoff rather than left to fire mid-phase: six deliverables plus an adversarial
pass do not fit half a day, and LexOS stays PAUSED all cycle so there is no live site to
probe. A row's outcome is therefore recorded evidence, and NOT-CHECKED is a first-class
answer rather than a failure to render.

rows.what: Terms and Conditions reachable at a stable public URL
Privacy Policy reachable at a stable public URL
Shipping / delivery policy, stating digital delivery where that is what is sold
Contact Us page carrying a real address, an email and a phone number
Cancellation and Refunds policy with a stated window

rows.condition: an additional e-commerce site, where the provider asks for an About Us page
rows.what: About Us page naming the operating entity

rows.condition: an additional e-commerce site, where the provider asks for pricing details
rows.what: Pricing details page stating the all-inclusive amount
